JIRA:KAFKA-20995
Release: TBD
Summary
The async consumer has repeatedly entered busy loops when a timer reaches zero while another state blocks the related work. The current numeric wait says when to poll again, but it cannot say whether time can make the work eligible or another event must occur first. Existing fixes replace the zero with another duration, which can make correctness depend on that duration's configuration.
This KIP introduces the internalManagerPollConditiontype withready(),after(...), andidle(). Each request-managerpoll()returns its outgoing requests and the condition for the next manager pass. The same manager decision can govern request admission and network scheduling. The network thread combines all manager conditions and applies the existing network-poll bounds. Public APIs, protocols, and thread topology remain unchanged. The internal per-managerRequestManager.maximumTimeToWait(long)method becomesapplicationPollCondition(long); the application-facingApplicationEventHandler.maximumTimeToWait()path remains unchanged.
Motivation
The async consumer has repeatedly entered a busy loop when a timer reaches zero while another state prevents the related work from continuing. The loop polls the same request managers, gets the same zero wait, and immediately starts again.
Today, each request manager returns outgoing requests and one numeric wait. The network thread uses the minimum:java
0starts another iteration immediately, a finite value schedules a timed iteration, andLong.MAX_VALUEadds no earlier deadline.
The application wait follows the same numeric model. Each manager returns a duration fromRequestManager.maximumTimeToWait(long). The network thread publishes the minimum ascachedMaximumTimeToWait, and the application thread uses it to limit its wait.

The following issues share the same pattern: work is blocked, but its timer still contributes zero.
